title: Triangulated Koszul comparison and twisted cup pairing for lattice actions
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $r\geq0$, let $D=\mathbf Z^r$ be discrete, and let $\mathcal A_R(D)$ be the category of internal $R$-modules with $D$-action [def-sfb-condensed-action-module, sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Use ordinary derived categories and derived invariants [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. For a module $P$ whose commuting action operators are $T_1,\ldots,T_r$, use the finite cochain complex $K_R(P;T)$, its signs, and its invariant inclusion from [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution]. For a bounded-below complex $P^\bullet$ of such modules, let $K_R(P^\bullet;T)$ denote the total complex of these finite Koszul complexes, with differential $d_K+(-1)^a d_P$ in Koszul degree $a$.

These total complexes induce a triangulated functor $\mathsf K_R:D^+(\mathcal A_R(D))\to D^+(\operatorname{Mod}_R)$. The natural Koszul comparisons of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] admit a simultaneous choice extending to an isomorphism of triangulated functors
$$\lambda:\mathsf K_R\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_{R,D}.$$
In particular, for every short exact sequence of equivariant modules, the comparison identifies the connecting morphism of its termwise exact Koszul sequence with the image under $R\Gamma_{R,D}$ of its canonical short-exact-sequence connecting morphism. It retains the invariant-inclusion normalization and is the identity for $r=0$.

For this same choice of $\lambda$, let $B$ be a commutative internal $R$-algebra with commuting $R$-algebra automorphisms $T_i$. Assume $B$ is flat over $R$, meaning that $B\otimes_R-$ is exact on internal modules. Write $K_B=K_R(B;T)$. The bounded complex $K_B$ is K-flat, meaning that tensoring it with any acyclic complex gives an acyclic total complex. There is a chain pairing $\star:K_B\otimes_R K_B\to K_B$ given, for homogeneous tuples $x\in K_B^p$, $y\in K_B^q$ and $|I|=p+q$, by
$$(x\star y)_I=\sum_{A\sqcup C=I,\ |A|=p}\epsilon(A,C)\,x_A\,T_A(y_C),\qquad T_A=\prod_{i\in A}T_i,$$
where $\epsilon(A,C)=(-1)^{\#\{(a,c)\in A\times C:c<a\}}$, and the empty product of operators is the identity. The invariant unit $R[0]\to K_B$ is $1_B$ in Koszul degree zero. In the derived category, with the ordinary tensor of the K-flat model representing derived tensor, this pairing satisfies
$$\lambda_B\circ Q(\star)=\operatorname{cup}_B\circ(\lambda_B\otimes_R^{\mathrm L}\lambda_B).$$
Here $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms and $\operatorname{cup}_B:R\Gamma_{R,D}(B)\otimes_R^{\mathrm L}R\Gamma_{R,D}(B)\to R\Gamma_{R,D}(B)$ is the canonical derived cup product induced by the equivariant multiplication of $B$. For $B=R$ with the trivial action, $\operatorname{cup}_R$ is the unital derived cup product on $R\Gamma_{R,D}(R[0])$ of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. The comparison sends the invariant unit to the canonical derived unit. No flatness, characteristic, or nonzero-ring hypothesis is imposed on $R$.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}_R$ and $\mathcal E=\mathcal A_R(D)$. By [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] these are Grothendieck abelian, forgetting is exact and detects exactness, and the exact trivial-action functor $t:\mathcal M\to\mathcal E$ is left adjoint to $\Gamma$. In each Koszul degree $a$, $K^a$ is a finite biproduct of the underlying-module functor; kernels and cokernels are componentwise, so $K^a$ is exact. The differential of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] is natural in equivariant maps and squares to zero. Totalizing with $d_K+(-1)^a d_P$ therefore defines an additive functor on bounded-below complexes.

proof.text: For a chain homotopy $h:P\to Q[-1]$, put $H|_{K^a(P^b)}=(-1)^aK^a(h^b)$. The horizontal terms in $dH+Hd$ cancel, and the vertical terms are $K^a(dh+hd)$, so totalization respects homotopy. For a quasi-isomorphism $f$, each fixed-$a$ column $K^a(f)$ is a quasi-isomorphism by exactness. The bicomplexes vanish for $a<0$ and for $b$ below a common integer. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-total-column-comparison] gives that $K(f)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Consequently $K$ descends to $\mathsf K_R$ on $D^+$; its output is bounded below since $0\leq a\leq r$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary open direct image: agent expansion of the discrete-lattice calculation below the tame-boundary route.

proof.text: Use the shift comparison $K(P[1])\to K(P)[1]$ that multiplies Koszul degree $a$ by $(-1)^a$. For $f:P\to Q$, use the cone convention $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^n=Q^n\oplus P^{n+1}$, with differential $(q,p)\mapsto(d_Qq+fp,-d_Pp)$. The map $K(\operatorname{Cone}f)\to\operatorname{Cone}(Kf)$ is identity on $K^aQ$ and multiplication by $(-1)^a$ on $K^aP[1]$. The horizontal differential on that second summand changes sign because $a$ increases by one; the vertical differential and off-diagonal $f$ term acquire precisely the displayed cone signs. It commutes with the inclusion of $KQ$ and, with the preceding shift comparison, the projection to $KP[1]$. Thus $K$ preserves cone triangles and descends as a triangulated functor under the cone-triangle definition of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text:
For an injective $J\in\mathcal E$, its degree-zero injective resolution computes $R\Gamma(J)=\Gamma(J)[0]$, by [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality]. The normalized comparison in [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] consequently says that the actual inclusion $\Gamma(J)[0]\to K(J)$ is a quasi-isomorphism: after localization its composite with that isomorphism is the identity of $\Gamma(J)[0]$. For a bounded-below $P$, take a monomorphic quasi-isomorphism $s:P\to J$ with bounded-below injective terms using [lem-weil-pbc-complex-injective-resolution-mono]; enough injectives follows from [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Each row inclusion just described is a quasi-isomorphism. The row version of [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-total-column-comparison] yields a quasi-isomorphism $b_J:\Gamma(J)\to K(J)$. Define
$$\lambda_P=Q(b_J)^{-1}Q(Ks):QK(P)\longrightarrow Q\Gamma(J)=R\Gamma(P).$$

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary open direct image: agent expansion of the discrete-lattice calculation below the tame-boundary route.

proof.text: A chain map $P\to P'$ lifts along the monomorphic resolution of $P$ to a map $J\to J'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso]. Any two lifts are homotopic by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy]. The maps $b_J$ commute with every such lift on complexes, and step 2 sends the lift homotopies to total homotopies. The normalized resolution comparison [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality] therefore makes $\lambda$ independent of resolutions and natural, including after localization. For a lifted map $J\to J'$, its cone is again bounded below and termwise injective. That same cited lemma computes the canonical derived cone triangle on this cone. The cone isomorphism of step 3 is identity on Koszul degree zero, so it commutes with $b$ and the invariant inclusions. Hence $\lambda$ respects the specified shifts and cone triangles. This proves an isomorphism of triangulated functors, and therefore compatibility with the canonical connecting arrow of any short exact sequence. Exactness of the $K^a$ identifies its image triangle with that of the termwise exact Koszul sequence.

proof.text: For a module $P$, both maps from $P^D[0]$ into $K(J)$ put the same invariant section in $J^0$ and zero elsewhere. Thus the comparison of step 4 has exactly the invariant-inclusion normalization of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution], and supplies a simultaneous choice of those module comparisons. For $r=0$, $K$ and $\Gamma$ are the identity and $b_J=1_J$; under the normalized derived identity, the formula is the identity on $P$. This also fixes its restriction to modules.

proof.text: Let $L^{-a}=\bigoplus_{|I|=a,v\in D}R[v,I]$, with differential the integral boundary of [lem-sfb-integral-lattice-cubical-contraction], now read as a cochain differential from $-a$ to $-a+1$. Translation acts on $v$. Replace each integer coefficient in that lemma's contraction by the same multiple of an identity morphism; finite support on each basis vector makes every map a coproduct map. This gives a nonequivariant homotopy between $1_L$ and the vertex section followed by $\varepsilon:L\to tR$. After tensoring with any complex $X$, $h\otimes1$ gives the same homotopy identity; the cross terms cancel by the total tensor sign of [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy]. In particular $L\otimes tX\to tX$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Forgetting detects this by [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. The same contraction shows that $L$ is K-flat: $L\otimes X$ is homotopy equivalent, after forgetting, to $X$, and is acyclic when $X$ is acyclic.

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary open direct image: agent expansion of the discrete-lattice calculation below the tame-boundary route.

proof.text:
Put $c_a=(-1)^{a(a+1)/2}$. For $x\in K^a(P^b)$ define an equivariant map
$$E_P:tK(P)\otimes L\longrightarrow P,\qquad E_P(x\otimes[v,I])=(-1)^{ab}c_aT^vx_I\quad(|I|=a),$$
and put it zero on the other Koszul/chain-degree pairs. Here $T^v=\prod_iT_i^{v_i}$ and $K(P)$ has trivial action. Translation of $v$ proves equivariance. To check the chain equation, identify the degree-$a,b$ component with equivariant maps $L^{-a}\to P^b$, multiplied by $\theta_{a,b}=(-1)^{ab}c_a$. The usual Hom differential is $df=d_Pf-(-1)^{a+b}f\partial$. The identities $\theta_{a,b+1}=(-1)^a\theta_{a,b}$ and $\theta_{a+1,b}=(-1)^{a+b+1}\theta_{a,b}$ identify it with $d_K+(-1)^ad_P$. Evaluation then has the stated chain equation. All assertions can be checked on each generator after every profinite base change, so they give morphisms of internal modules. On $t\Gamma(P)\otimes L$, evaluation is exactly the invariant inclusion composed with $1\otimes\varepsilon$: only $a=0$ and vertices survive.

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary open direct image: agent expansion of the discrete-lattice calculation below the tame-boundary route.

proof.text:
The adjunction $t\dashv\Gamma$ of step 1 has its normalized derived adjunction by [lem-sfb-resolving-derived-adjunction-normalization]: the left resolving class can be all complexes since $t$ is exact. Unbounded injective replacements exist by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective]. On a bounded-below injective $J$, its derived counit is $t\Gamma(J)\to J$, by the chain-transpose clause of the normalization lemma. Step 8 gives the commuting chain square with horizontal arrows $t\Gamma(J)\otimes L\to tK(J)\otimes L$ and $t\Gamma(J)\to J$, and vertical arrows $1\otimes\varepsilon$ and $E_J$. The top arrow is a quasi-isomorphism since $b_J$ is one and $L$ is K-flat (step 7). The left arrow is a quasi-isomorphism by the contraction. Thus, in the derived category, the roof
$$tQK(P)\xleftarrow{1\otimes\varepsilon}Q(tK(P)\otimes L)\xrightarrow{E_P}P$$
is the derived counit composed with $t\lambda_P$, first for $J$ and then for $P$ by the naturality of evaluation and $s:P\to J$. This identifies the actual derived arrow; it does not infer equality from cohomology.

proof.text: For flat $B$, each term of $K_B$ is a finite sum of copies of $B$ and hence flat: tensor with it is a finite sum of exact functors. The internal-to-sectionwise equivalence [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] preserves flatness, total tensors and acyclicity. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] to this bounded complex on the small condensed site and transport back: $K_B$ is K-flat. The same reasoning on underlying modules proves that $tK_B$ is K-flat equivariantly, since forgetting creates exactness and the equivariant tensor has underlying tensor with diagonal action. Thus ordinary tensor models every derived tensor in the following evaluation calculation.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; transported to internal modules by the cited tensor equivalence.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-integral-cubical-chain-diagonal] and replace its integer entries by $R$-linear maps as in step 7. This gives a counital equivariant chain map $\Delta:L\to L\otimes_RL$. Define a bilinear map $\star$ by the formula in the statement. It is a chain map by an explicit twisted Leibniz identity: put $D_i=T_i-1$; then
$$D_i(xT_Ay)=D_i(x)T_{A\cup\{i\}}y+xT_A D_i(y)\quad(i\notin A).$$
For each ordered partition of $I\cup\{i\}$, group the differential terms according as $i$ is in the first or second factor. In the first group, moving $i$ through the ordered first block gives exactly the Koszul sign of $dx\star y$; in the second it passes all $p$ elements of the first block, adding $(-1)^p$, and gives $x\star dy$. The displayed identity supplies their coefficients. Therefore $d(x\star y)=dx\star y+(-1)^px\star dy$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary open direct image: agent expansion of the discrete-lattice calculation below the tame-boundary route.

proof.text:
Write $n=p+q$. Compare the two maps from $t(K_B\otimes K_B)\otimes L$ to $B$: evaluation after $t\star$, and multiplication after $\Delta$ and the two evaluations. On $x_A\otimes y_C\otimes[v,I]$ with $|A|=p$, $|C|=q$, both vanish unless $A\sqcup C=I$. The first is
$$c_n\epsilon(A,C)T^v(x_A)T^{v+u_A}(y_C).$$
In the second, the relevant diagonal term is $\epsilon(A,C)[v,A]\otimes[v+u_A,C]$. Moving $y_C$ past $[v,A]$ contributes $(-1)^{pq}$, and the evaluations contribute $c_pc_q$. These agree because $c_n=(-1)^{pq}c_pc_q$. Thus the maps agree on every summand and hence as chain maps. The counit identity $(\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta=\varepsilon$ identifies the left arrows of their evaluation roofs. Since $K_B$ is K-flat and the augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms, this is the derived equality between evaluation after $\star$ and multiplication after the two counit evaluations.

proof.text: For the ambient monoidal constructions, identify internal modules with section modules using [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison], and actions with module sheaves on the small action site using [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation]. The latter equivalence also identifies tensors: both are the sheafification of the balanced local pure tensors, and an arrow $(f,a)$ acts on $m\otimes n$ as $a f^*m\otimes a f^*n$. The action site is small in the chosen universe. Thus [lem-trf-site-functorial-flat-resolution] provides functorial flat resolutions in both categories, and their tensor is closed by [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. The trivial-action functor $t$ is exact, left adjoint, and strong monoidal, with identity underlying tensor and unit identifications. It preserves flat objects since forgetting detects exactness. Apply [lem-sfb-exact-flat-tensor-derived-counit-comparison] to obtain its normalized derived tensor identification. The canonical cup is the adjunction transpose of multiplication after the tensor of the two derived counits. Step 9 identifies the evaluation roofs with these counits after $t\lambda_B$. Step 12 says exactly that the transposes of $\lambda_BQ(\star)$ and $\operatorname{cup}_B(\lambda_B\otimes^{\mathrm L}\lambda_B)$ coincide. The adjunction bijection proves their equality. Evaluation of $1_B$ is $\varepsilon$ followed by $R\to B$, since $T^v1_B=1_B$; its transpose is the derived unit. For trivial $B=R$, this is the cup and unit of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus].

proof.text: When $r=0$, only the empty partition occurs, $c_0=1$, and all evaluation, augmentation and diagonal formulas are identity or multiplication. For $r=1$, $\Delta[v,\{1\}]=[v,\varnothing]\otimes[v,\{1\}]+[v,\{1\}]\otimes[v+u_1,\varnothing]$; accordingly $x^0\star y^1=x^0y^1$ and $x^1\star y^0=x^1T_1(y^0)$, whose differential is $(T_1-1)(xy)=(T_1-1)x\,T_1y+x(T_1-1)y$. No division or alternating average was used. All formulas hold for the zero ring, the zero module, and characteristic two (where the signs become equal).

tool_uses.why: Finite-strip bicomplex comparison supplies the generic total quasi-isomorphism theorem; the lattice unit gives only its degree-zero module instance.
Normalized resolution and cone comparisons identify the specified triangulated derived maps, a generic homological-algebra input absent from the lattice unit.
Generic existence of monomorphic bounded-below injective replacements is needed for actual chain lifts; no lattice-unit statement supplies it.
Enough injectives for the given Grothendieck action category is a general existence theorem, not a lattice calculation.
Extends maps to the chosen injective replacements, a generic chain-level tool.
Generic homotopy uniqueness makes the comparison independent of all lifts.
Supplies the signed total tensor on homotopy categories used to tensor the explicit contraction.
The transpose-normalized derived adjunction identifies evaluation with the canonical counit, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism of cohomology.
Unbounded replacement existence verifies the ambient hypothesis of the generic derived adjunction lemma.
Transports the ringed-site K-flat criterion to the actual internal tensor without changing coefficients.
Generic ringed-site bounded-flat criterion proves K-flatness of the finite lattice cochain complex.
Generic normalized exact derived tensor comparison identifies inflation of a derived tensor with the tensor of inflations.
Generic small-ringed-site flat resolution existence verifies both ambient hypotheses of the exact derived monoidal comparison.
Generic tensor-Hom adjunction gives the closed module tensor on both the coefficient and the action site.
